correctness.rationale: For every integer d>=3, the rotated orthonormal coordinates t=(x1+z)/sqrt(2), v=(x1-z)/sqrt(2), w=(x2,...,x_(d-1)) split z>=0 and z<=0. The allowable w-ball squared radii factor exactly as (1-sqrt(2)*t)(1+sqrt(2)*v) for v<=t and (1+sqrt(2)*t)(1-sqrt(2)*v) for v>=t; integration over the correct [-1/sqrt(2),1/sqrt(2)] support proves A(t)=2sqrt(2)*kappa_(d-2)/d*(1-2t^2)^((d-2)/2). The volume 2*kappa_(d-1)/d, h=1/sqrt(2), and beta substitution give the claimed normalized F_d. The affine hyperplane Jacobian is |det T|/lambda with T^Tu=lambda*u*, and all factors cancel. For d=3 the ellipsoid value is 3*pi^2/16. Positive binomial coefficients yield B(1/2,5/4)>(pi/2)*(8939/8192); exact rational arithmetic proves F3-3*pi^2/16>893631283/46976204800>1/100. All quantifiers and endpoint cases d>=3, t=+-1/sqrt(2), centered linear-image scope checked. Independent 60-decimal geometric integrations at d=3,4,7,11 and t=0,.237,.6 matched the profile to relative error <1e-50, and the rational bound was checked with fractions. The infinite family follows from symbolic integrals, not from these samples.
residual_risks: No proof is claimed about maximization over bisector directions or all centrally symmetric bodies; numerical tests are corroborative.

Computing a genuinely oblique direction is therefore motivated. The all-dimensional exact hyperplane-section profile and affine-invariant beta constant supply a reusable geometric benchmark, and the concrete d=3 gap >1/100 is sharper than the qualitative 2026 preprint baseline, with a rigorous positive certificate. This is not a claim of an optimal cone direction, general conjecture or groundbreaking theorem. The old conjecture motivation is weakened by a 2026 general-preprint argument, yet precise oblique section data remain independently useful. The result is stronger than a mere parameter substitution or unmotivated small numerical gain because it determines the whole section profile and an exact directional invariant for all d>=3.
